summary.headline: LMW Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 30% to ₹1,153 crore and PBT reached ₹204 crore, with TMD order book near ₹3,400 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹1,153 crore versus ₹815 crore a year earlier (about 30% growth), and H1 revenue was ₹2,045 crore, up 33%. PBT was ₹204 crore against ₹93 crore in the prior-year period. Textile Machinery Division (TMD) grew 38% YoY in Q2 to ₹639 crore, while the Machine Tool Division and Foundry H1 turnover rose to ₹794 crore from ₹555 crore. Management was cautious on textile demand because of input cost inflation and supply chain issues, and more positive on machine tools and ATC.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY; +32% vs ₹482 crore in the previous quarter
vs ₹555 crore; Foundry is 9% of this

segments.name: Textile Machinery (TMD)
segments.commentary: Q2 turnover ₹639 crore (+38% YoY); H1 ₹1,121 crore with profit ₹48 crore. Order book about ₹3,400 crore, of which active order book about ₹2,600 crore. H1 sales mix: 67% domestic, 8% exports, 25% spares; capacity utilisation about 60%.

segments.name: Machine Tool Division (MTD) and Foundry
segments.commentary: H1 turnover ₹794 crore, of which Foundry is 9%. Utilisation 75-80%. Management expects around 50% growth this year and says it is adding capacity.

segments.name: ATC (aerospace, defence and composites)
segments.commentary: H1 turnover ₹135 crore (+39%). Utilisation about 70%. Order book about ₹1,000 crore, roughly 70% metallics and 30% composites. Segment margin cited at about 22%.

segments.name: LMW Global (Dubai) and LMW China
segments.commentary: LMW Global H1 turnover ₹100 crore with order book about ₹163 crore; LMW China H1 turnover ₹36 crore with order book about ₹128 crore. Management cited a loss in the overseas holding last year (about ₹29.5 crore at LMW Global per annual report, which management did not directly confirm).

guidance_outlook: MTD expected to grow about 50% in the current year, per management.
Capex for the year is planned to be broadly in line with depreciation, with some assets to come in on lease.
ATC: the ₹150 crore investment is planned under a Tamil Nadu government MoU, but there is no commissioning timeline yet.
Infinium land JV (4.2 acres): realisation about 25%, value ₹20-24 crore, over 24-30 months, with some realisation this year and some next year.
Management said it will take only orders it can execute, adding capacity to match, because contracts carry penalty clauses.
capex_capacity: MTD: capacity expansion of about 10% on a base of 6,750 machines, with ₹10 crore investment; this is a repurposed existing unit for assembly and is described as a statutory third-unit filing. Management says it will expand further at 80-85% utilisation.
MTD mix: about 76% turning centres and 23-24% machining centres; machining centres are growing faster.
ATC: the ₹150 crore investment is yet to be deployed. Management cites an asset-turn rule of thumb of about 1:1 to 1:1.3 (turnover to investment).
TMD utilisation about 60%; ATC about 70%; MTD 75-80%.
Overseas: investments in LMW Holding rose from ₹206 crore to ₹377 crore, and management said this is for capacity and market expansion (for example Africa and GCC).
demand_pricing: TMD: management is cautious. Input costs for commodities, copper, aluminium and electronics are rising, and there is a second-order war impact. TMD is on fixed-price contracts with no current price pass-through, though a price discussion is active and VAVE cost programmes are under way.
TMD order book about ₹3,400 crore; net order inflow up about ₹200 crore in the quarter; about 70% of orders are project orders.
MTD: order inflow is consistent. Demand is driven by China+1 and machine upgrades. Auto is still a little over 50% of MTD sales, with defence, EMS and tooling expanding.
Indian machine tool market about 17,000-18,000 machines and about $2-2.5 billion by value. Imports are about 40-45% by volume and 50-55% by value, and are declining as domestic makers grow.
Lakshmi Auto Winder: launched and sold to a few southern customers, with ramp-up expected next year. Market is roughly ₹1,500 crore-plus, since winding is about 25-30% of spinning mill capex.
Management said export markets like Bangladesh and Turkey are challenged, and overseas losses reflect low topline. ATC is 90% export historically; domestic defence is now being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: ATC capacity, peak revenue from current and planned capex, and commissioning timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is about 70%. The asset-turn rule of thumb is 1:1 to 1.3. No timeline has been given for the new investment, which will be announced at an appropriate time.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for TMD EBITDA margin, given the textile tailwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tailwind is more apt for MTD. TMD is cautious because of cost inflation and supply chain issues. There is no price pass-through yet, and VAVE is under way.

qa_highlights.question: MTD capacity expansion of only 10% when demand grows about 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: The expansion is a repurposed unit and is statutory filing-driven, not a calibrated expansion. Management said it will keep adding capacity at 80-85% utilisation, and that the ₹10 crore figure understates the ecosystem.

qa_highlights.question: Overseas losses and LMW Holding investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Overseas losses reflect weak topline in Bangladesh and Turkey, plus high-cost locations. Order books of ₹163 crore (Global) and ₹128 crore (China) will be executed over the next 6-12 months. The ~₹200 crore sent overseas was used to buy the China subsidiary and returned to India.

qa_highlights.question: What does the ATC defence order book look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name specific programmes. It said it covers structures, assemblies, special processes and machining, but not electronics. Management said it is not into forging.

qa_highlights.question: Fixed cost trend and capex for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited cost control, digitisation and automation, and VAVE for better COGS. Capex will be broadly in line with depreciation, with some leased assets.

risks_watch: TMD margins: H1 profit ₹48 crore on ₹1,121 crore revenue, with cost inflation and no price pass-through yet on fixed-price contracts.
Overseas subsidiaries (LMW Global, LMW China) remain loss-making with weak topline; order books are ₹163 crore and ₹128 crore.
ATC ₹150 crore investment has no commissioning timeline, and ATC's capacity constraint (about 70% utilisation) is a watch item.
Capacity additions in MTD are small (about 10%) against management's ~50% growth view. Watch the actual capacity plan and utilisation.
Management declined to answer questions on demerger, promoter stake, and programme-level defence details.
summary.management_tone: Confident on MTD and ATC growth, and cautious on TMD, where management repeatedly cited uncertainty from input cost inflation, war-related second-order effects and supply chain constraints. Evasive on several specifics (ATC capex timing, defence programmes, demerger and stake questions).
key_quotes: So, it is not a calibrated expansion; it is a planned expansion.
We cannot take orders which we cannot execute because there is enough penalties available in this contract clauses.
I think you can always turn on the tap with the multiple shifts, right?

adds.what: MTD capacity +10% on base of 6,750 machines (repurposed existing unit for assembly, ₹10 crore)
ATC ₹150 crore investment under Tamil Nadu MoU, no commissioning timeline

growth.why: Management guides Machine Tool Division growth of about 50% this year, backed by a 10% MTD capacity add (₹10 crore, minor) and a TMD order book of about ₹3,400 crore (₹2,600 crore active), though the ₹150 crore ATC investment has no commissioning timeline and TMD is cautious on input costs and fixed-price contracts.
